title: Fruit Salad without Citrus with Pudding

content.title: About
content.content: Fruit salad without citrus with pudding is a mix of fresh berries, apples, pears, bananas and other non‑citrus fruits, tossed with a smooth vanilla pudding (item 4061). The salad is served chilled and works as a light dessert or snack.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The salad contains no citrus, making it safe for people allergic to lemon, orange or grapefruit.
The pudding base is made from milk, starch and vanilla extract, giving the dish a creamy texture.
Apples and pears stay crisp thanks to a short chill time in the refrigerator.
Bananas add natural sweetness, allowing the recipe to use less added sugar.
The dish can be prepared in 15‑20 minutes, which is why it’s popular in cafés and cafeterias.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Apples, pears and bananas provide vitamins B1, B2 and B6, supporting metabolic processes.

items.title: Good source of dietary fiber
items.content: The fruit mix supplies soluble and insoluble fiber that promotes healthy digestion.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: The salad contains almost no fat, and the pudding is made with skim milk, keeping it light.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Berries such as blueberries and strawberries are high in anthocyanins, which protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Immune support
items.content: Vitamin C from the berries (non‑citrus) helps boost the immune system.

items.title: Allergy to specific fruits
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to apples, pears or certain berries; a test portion is advisable.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Bananas and berries are naturally sweet, so people monitoring blood glucose should consider the total carbohydrate load.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: Certain fruits can increase stomach acidity; those with gastritis should choose milder options.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the salad chilled in individual cups or bowls. Before serving, garnish with fresh mint leaves or a sprinkle of chopped nuts for extra crunch.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared salad in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours. The pudding may separate, so give it a gentle stir before serving.
